thread:
mira: noticing sustained small bursts from a set of IPs rotating UA strings, CPU on inference proxies creeping up. 503s on a few clients. possible low-and-slow probing. seeing KV cache eviction noise.
pranav: can you paste the top sample logs?
mira: here - `edge-proxy | 1998765432 | src=3.142.5.9 ua=Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Bot/2.1) path=/v1/generate status=503 latency_ms=410` repeated across /generate and /embeddings with different UA and same ASN.
alex: I see similar in metrics: 95th p99 token latency + backend CPU saturating. Not a full volumetric DDoS but wasteful small requests causing expensive model loads.
mira: agree. pattern: many distinct UA, low requests per IP, high concurrency across many origins -> evasion.
julia: propose short circuit: activate adaptive token-based rate limit and add WAF rule to drop requests with suspicious header patterns. can we do a quick canary?
pranav: deploying a dynamic rate-limit policy now to edge: `rl-action: 429; window: 60s; requests: 12; key: client_ip+route` pushing to canary region us-west-2.
deploy-bot: rate-limit-policy/rl-1998 applied to namespace=edge-canary by @pranav at 1998765485
alex: also creating WAF rule: match rotating UA regex + high accept header churn -> challenge/captcha. snippet: ```waf_rule {
  id: "suspicious-ua-rotor-1"
  match: "User-Agent: /Bot|curl|python-requests|Mozilla\/5\.0.*\(compatible.*Bot/\)/i"
  action: "challenge"
}```
mira: good. we should also enable stricter KV cache TTL for those request keys to avoid thrash. set kv.cache.ttl.short=true for flagged flows.
sarah: heads-up for support: some low-volume customers on shared proxies might see 429s briefly. draft comms?
comms-bot: draft: "We applied temporary rate limits and WAF challenges to mitigate suspicious probing activity. If you experience errors, contact support with request-id and we'll whitelist safe traffic." Want to send to affected customers?
julia: hold on escalation. first confirm no legitimate partners affected. alex can we run a quick query for whitelisted API keys in the hitset?
alex: running: `select api_key, count(*) from edge_logs where rule_id='suspicious-ua-rotor-1' group by api_key limit 50` -> 0 matches for whitelisted keys.
mira: ok safe to broaden rollout. prio next: audit logs & RBAC. we need an audit event for the WAF/rate-limit change and ensure only sec-eng and netops can modify rules.
pranav: opened PR #3421 to add RBAC: `role: sec-eng` and `role: netops` -> permissions: waf:modify, rate-limit:modify. link: https://git.internal/r/3421
alex: also enable KMS envelope logging for policy key access so we can trace who applied the policy. KMS team: ensure CloudKMS audit logs retained 90 days.
julia: post-incident action items: 1) tune UA regex and false-positive review 2) permanent adaptive RL on per-route 3) add customer-facing status page note if sustained 4) run retrospective with sec-eng+netops.
sarah: I'll prep a short support note and triage doc with steps for customers who report issues.
mira: thanks team. will keep monitoring. if metrics flatten in 10m, we revert canary to prod config with same rules.
deploy-bot: rollout to prod-edge scheduled at 1998766120 by @pranav (manual approval required).
comms-bot: internal incident stub created: INC-1998. Adding involved owners mira, praj, alex, sarah.
pranav: closing loop: initial mitigation reduced p99 latency by 48% and CPU by 35% in canary. keep rate-limit in prod with 60s sliding window.
mira: filing postmortem checklist and tagging for RBAC audit and KMS retention. will update INC-1998 with notes and timeline. :white_check_mark:
